1.

MCRC no. 8512/2025 and MCRC no. 3717/2025 have been restored in view of the order dated 21/08/2025 passed by the Supreme Court in SLP (Cri) Diary no. 42639/2025.
2.

This fifth bail application (MCRC no.40353/2025) has been filed by applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 for grant of regular bail in connection with Crime No.
850/2023 registered at Police Station- Agar, District- - Agar Malwa (M.P.) for offence punishable under Sections 420 and 409 of the IPC.

entities.text: Police Station- Agar, District- - Agar Malwa
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant is in judicial custody since 25/12/2023.
3. Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 03/07/2024 passed in MCRC no. 14252/2024.
His second bail application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 28/08/2024 passed in MCRC no. 36711/2024.

His third bail application was allowed vide order dated 14/02/2025 passed in MCRC no. 3717/2025 subject deposit of Rs. 20,13,650/-
before the trial Court before his release.
Applicant Mukesh applied for relaxation of the condition of bail by filing forth bail application.

The co-ordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated 05/05/2025 passed in MCRC no. 8512/2025, extended facility of three installments for deposit of Rs. 15,00,000/- and granted bail subject to deposit of Rs. 5,13,650/-.
The applicant assailed the order dated 05/05/2025 before the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court, vide order dated 21/08/2025 passed in SLP (Cri) Diary no. 42639/2025, directed as under :
"8.

However, since disposal of the prayer for regular bail based on the statement of the learned counsel for the petitioner resulted in no real examination of his prayer for bail by the High Court on merits, we are of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29071 3 MCRC-40353-2025 considered opinion that interest of justice would be sufficiently served if we set aside the impugned orders, direct revival of the application for bail and request the High Court to consider such application for bail afresh in accordance with law, on its own merits.
Ordered accordingly."
4. Accordingly, the bail applications are being considered on merits of the case.

5. Heard the arguments.
6.
Perused the grounds for grant of bail stated in the application, case diary and the relevant material on record.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the alleged offence merely on the basis of statement of co-accused Kamal in police custody and his own incriminating statement before the police.

sentences.text: recovery has been made at the instance of applicant.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.
Co-accused Kamal has been extended the benefit of bail v i d e order dated 07/08/2024 passed in MCRC no. 32201/2024.
The material relied by the prosecution against the applicant is identical in nature.
The final report has been submitted on completion of investigation.
The applicant is in custody since 25/12/2023.
The trial is not progressing at appropriate pace.
Only one witness, out of 36 enlisted witnesses for the prosecution could be examined till date.
The applicant has no resources to comply with the bail order regarding deposit of the money, therefore, he continues to be in jail.
The long Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant and the dependent family.
Applicant is ready to cooperate in the trial.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the application NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:29071 4 MCRC-40353-2025 on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.

However,
after going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.

9. According to the material available on case diary, Mukesh (applicant) and Kamal were working as custodian in C.M.S. Company for loading cash in A.T.M. Machines of SBI, BOI, ICICi Bank, IDBI Bank, BTI Bank, Branch Agar Malwa.
Mukesh and Kamal (substitute custodian) have misappropriated Rs. 40,10,700/-.
The main custodian Balwant, on return after leave, informed Shri Neeraj Bhat, Branch Manager of C.M.S. Company about loss of money in ATMs.
Neeraj Bhat conducted audit and reported the matter to the Police Station - Agar.
The Police Station - Agar registered FIR for offence punishable under section 420 and 409 of the IPC against Mukesh and Kamal.
Mukesh was apprehended on 25/12/2023.
He is in custody ever since.
No recovery has been made during investigation.
Mukesh had informed that he had spent the embezzled money in On-line Gaming.
However, the money trail was traced.
The trial is under way.
As per the status report received from the trial Court, only one prosecution witness, out of 36 enlisted witnesses could be examined till date.
The trial is delayed and would take sufficient time to conclude.
The veracity of prosecution and complicity of the applicant will be determined after evidence in the trial.
10. As informed, the applicant is aged around 23 years.
He was working in private job.
He has family responsibilities.
Considering these aspects, there appears to be no possibility of fleeing from justice.

In absence of any criminal antecedent, considering the socio-economic status of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29071 5 MCRC-40353-2025 applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with evidence or influencing the witnesses by the applicant.
There appears to be no compelling reason to continue incarceration of the applicant.

However, the observations,
herein-above, are recorded for present application only.

11. Considering the rival contentions and overall circumstances of the case, in the light of aforestated facts, but without commenting on the merits, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
